newsitem.title: USA: Cook Inlet oil lease sale gets approval in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Cook Inlet oil lease sale gets approval in Alaska.

text.p: A controversial federal oil and gas lease sale for Alaska's Cook Inlet has received final approval, the U.S. Minerals Management Service said on Thursday.
The sale, for federal waters in the outercontinental shelf of the inlet, will be held on June 11, the agency said.

The offshore lease sale acreage was slashed after protests from activists who said oil and gas drilling in the lower part of the inlet would harm the area's ecology and interfere with commercial fishing and recreational activities, the agency said.

"The decision to proceed with the sale was made after we considered all comments received from fishing groups, natural gas and oil companies, industry support companies, environmental organizations, state and local governments and numerous local residents," minerals management director Cynthia Quarterman said in a statement.
The sale area was reduced to 430,000 acres from the original 2 million acres considered for oil and gas leasing.
Fishermen, environmentalists, Democratic Gov. Tony Knowles and some residents wanted the sale canceled.

Their concerns prompted the federal agency to impose some additional protections in addition to the acreage reduction, such as a prohibition of off-loading from oil tankers in the inlet, said Knowles spokesman Bob King.
"We're pleased that the Minerals Management Service considered the concerns of lower Cook Inlet residents," King said.

However, the Knowles administration was disappointed that the agency did not delete from the sale all offshore tracts south of the Kenai Peninsula town of Ninilchik, King said. Knowles has vowed to bar any state oil and gas lease sales for offshore tracts south of that town, King said.
Oil company officials, meanwhile, have said they were disappointed at the reduction in acreage for the upcoming federal Cook Inlet lease sale.
